title.narrative: Development and Implementation to support the India-EU Water Partnership - phase II

description.narrative: Action to strengthen knowledge and experience exchange between public and private sector stakeholders in EUMS and India with regard to the water sector (including River Basin Management), thereby facilitating a progressive convergence by India towards relevant EU policies and standards on water management. This will be achieved by sharing best practices and learnings, by promoting policy dialogue, joint research and business cooperation between India, the EU and the EUMS in the water sector.

Second reporting period1. The development of the National Framework on Safe Reuse of Treated Water SRTW under the IEWP Action has been commended by Mr. Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Minister of Jal Shakti Government of India during a meeting on 22nd November 2022. He mentioned that Framework on SRTW will serve as a guidance document to the State Governments to develop their own policies to foster the reuse of treated water. The Minister instructed the NMCG officials to speed up the finalization of framework by incorporating the suggestions made by the Indian States. Further Minister advised IEWP Action to work on the development of business models for various end uses in India based on the success stories from the India and the EU to foster the implementation of the recommendations of the National Framework on SRTW. First reporting period1. A specific meeting was held on 26.11.2020 to present the Tapi River Basin Management Plan to the Secretary and other higher officials of the Ministry of Jal Shakti and Tapi Basin States. Secretary Mr. U. P. Singh Ministry of Jal Shakti has highly appreciated that the approach to identify the Key Water Management Issues tackled in the Tapi RBM Plan. He mentioned that contemporary Indian approaches of managing the rivers mainly consider water quantity in basins and its utilization practices associated issue that are also key importance are usually not integrated. He also appreciated the risk assessment approach in the Tapi RBM Plan. The Secretary asked the experts from the allied institutions of the Ministry of Jal Shakti and the basin States to provide feedback on the Tapi RBM Plan as well as on the procedures towards joint implementation of the Programme of Measures recommended in the Tapi RBM Plan. 2. On 8.3. 2021 a meeting was organized to brief the Honorable Minister Mr. Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Ministry of Jal Shakti on the development of National Framework on Safe Reuse of Treated Water. The Minister has appreciated the support provided under IEWP Action to develop the National Framework on Safe Reuse of Treated Water. Mr. Shekhawat mentioned that increasing water efficiency and recycling of water for reuse are very much needed In India as of now to contribute to decreasing the gap between water demand and water supply. The HOD EU Delegation in India gave the Opening Remarks.3. The EUIndia High Level Joint Working Group Meeting on Water Cooperation between the EU and Ministry of Jal Shakti 24 and 31 March 2021 was cochaired by Ms. Debashree Mukherjee Additional Secretary Ministry of Jal Shakti Ms. Astrid Schomaker Director Global Sustainable Development DG Environment European Commission. The cochair acknowledged the joint efforts good spirit and achievements under the IndiaEU Water Partnership the bilateral water cooperation and congratulated all participants for the good work. The Additional Secretary Ms. Mukherjee said that the EUIndia Joint Working Group Meeting has led to a much better understanding of the different policies in place in the EU and India as well as regarding the activities of the IndiaEU Water Partnership both as a project and as a vehicle for policy dialogue.

comment.narrative: 4 approaches agreed upon1 Further promotion of integrated RBM in India through the IEWP2 Approach for the development of the detailed Tapi RBM Plans including programme of measures for implementation3 Implementation strategy for ensuring adequate EFlows 4 Implementation strategy for treated wastewater reuse

With the development of Tapi RBM Plan a participatory planning mechanism involving the river basin states was established for the very first time in India. Further the RBM cycle based on the EU Water Framework Directive WFD is now established in India as an approach to develop RBM Plans evident from development replication of a similar approach in the Ramganga Basin. Furthermore the Ministry of Jal Shakti and its allied institutions appreciate the approach of developing the Programme of Measures for the Tapi basin based on the results of the Risk Assessment. This ensures that the measures proposed target specifically the key water management issues identified in the basin. IEWP Action contributed significantly to incorporate the ecological aspects into the Indian EFlows assessment which so far only focused on abiotic hydrology. This approach considers demands for environmental use when determining the adequate level of flows that should be ensured in rivers thereby contributing to biodiversity conservation.The draft SRTW Framework developed by the project offers guidance to the Indian States on how to develop new or realign existing statelevel policies to foster water reuse. The formal notification of the SRTW framework will give legal support to institutions processes and innovative technologies to promote wastewater reuse as well as the creation of a formal market and viable business and financial models. This contributes to global striving towards resource efficiency and circular economy.

Second reporting period1. Characterization of basin characterization of a basin is a process which evaluates and classifies the water bodies based on typologies and reference conditions with a perspective to use this as an existing baseline condition of a river basin. This baseline condition provides an overview regarding the pressures and drivers on water resources in the selected basin. The baseline condition facilitates the decision makers to prioritize the Key Water Management Issues in the basin and to take further steps accordingly towards improved basin governance in the context of integrated river basin management. 2. Pressure analysisRiver basin Management in India primarily focused on the development of water storage infrastructure and sewerage infrastructure as evident from early phase of Namami Gange Programme. However with the introduction of the RBM cycle based on the good practices of the EU WFD through India EU Water Partnership Action Key Water Management Issues were identified together with the basin states. Thereafter for the very time first time DPSIR framework is applied to carry out the pressure analysis for each KWMI in Tapi Basin followed by in Ramganga Basin. First reporting periodThe Ministry of Jal Shakti has upgraded the Tapi River Basin Committee as an RBM steering structure in March 2021. The committee is upgraded with additional members from the relevant water authorities and ministries from the Central and Tapi Basin States. The continued implementation of the RBM Cycle and revisiondetailing of the Tapi RBM Plan are clear mandates of the Committee. Hence an RBM practice that has been influenced by the IEWP Action is already in place.This upgraded Committee is an acknowledgement and recognition by the Government of India for the technical support provided under the framework of IEWP to develop and implement the RBM Plan based on the EU best practices.
